documents.title: Lightweight execution runtime
documents.text:
The public C++17 API in `FHN/Runtime.h` executes a named request when submitted.
It does not record a program or invoke a compiler. Contributions register
recipes with public-metadata applicability checks, deterministic priorities and
an execution callback. One recipe can produce several outputs, allocate a
preparation artifact, or compose other requests. The runtime has no built-in
arithmetic instruction vocabulary.

documents.title: Execution and resource contract
documents.text:
`Runtime::submit(Request)` selects the first applicable recipe, ordered by
descending priority and then registration order. An applicability decline may
try another recipe. Once execution begins, an exception is reported without
retrying a different implementation. Callers observe returned outputs only on
success. Providers must preserve escaped inputs; the generic core cannot police
mutability hidden inside arbitrary `std::any` payloads or roll back external
side effects.

documents.title: Execution and resource contract
documents.text:
`Value` is a shared immutable resource handle with an identity, format tag,
provider payload and strong dependencies. Copies share one charge. Resource
payloads are destroyed before their dependencies, so provider cleanup may use
the dependency storage. Handles can outlive their `Runtime`; native handles
also retain their backend context and loaded library. Releasing the last handle
releases its charge. A new encryption/import has a new identity even when its
shape and parameters match an existing input.

documents.title: Execution and resource contract
documents.text:
`makeValue` reserves the declared bytes **before** invoking its factory and
rolls back reservations on failure. Reentrant factories count their pending
reservation. The optional retained-memory budget is not a process-memory
limit: keys, context tables/scratch, callback temporaries, graph metadata and
allocator overhead are excluded. Native ciphertexts charge their actual fixed
reserved slab size, including spare components. Rotation artifacts charge
their snapshot and coefficient slabs. An explicit region reserves its entire
chosen workspace cap; executable statistics separately expose used workspace.

documents.title: Execution and resource contract
documents.text:
Diagnostics retain at most `max_trace_events` events (default 256); zero
disables them. Calls on a runtime and on a native context are synchronous and
must be serialized. No background queue, automatic cache, graph matching,
autotuning or global representation search is hidden in dispatch.

documents.title: Native execution and reusable state
documents.text:
`FHN/NativeRuntime.h` supplies a compute-only adapter. `NativeServices` can be
injected, or `loadNativeServices(path)` loads the genuine CPU CKKS plugin.
Neither services nor recipes hold a client or secret key. Trusted application
code separately encrypts inputs, prepares public evaluation keys and decrypts
outputs. Keys remain client-owned; expired keys cause evaluation to fail.

documents.title: Native execution and reusable state
documents.text:
Import copies the ciphertext. Subsequent mutation/freeing of the original
buffer cannot invalidate the runtime value. A rotation preparation owns a
canonical source snapshot and inverse-NTT c1 limbs. Each consumer applies its
own coefficient automorphism and basis conversion/key switch. It reuses inverse
transforms, not the entire hoisted key-switch decomposition. Its exact reserve
is `3 * active_q_limbs * polynomial_degree * sizeof(uint64_t)`.
The adapter checks source identity before reuse, including when the supplied
replacement has the same ciphertext layout. The raw optional C exports in
`FHN/fhn_prepared_api.h` instead operate on the owned snapshot directly.

documents.title: Native execution and reusable state
documents.text:
`op()` preserves physical FHN opcode semantics. `semantic()` is an explicitly
chosen application adapter for the eight circuit operations: multiplication
uses normalized HMULT; integer scale uses additions/negation without consuming
a level; fractional scale uses native scalar multiplication. Binary operands
can be lowered to a common level, but incompatible actual scales still fail.
This policy belongs to the native adapter, not the generic runtime.

documents.title: Optional compilation
documents.text:
Compilation is an explicit request with a node limit and finite workspace cap.
Prototype inputs contribute signatures; the executable does not retain their
data and may be rebound to fresh compatible inputs. Oversized or unsupported
regions leave immediate execution usable. There is no implicit “try the
compiler” step on ordinary requests. Compile-time graph metadata is bounded by
the node/input/output limits of the compiler, not charged as ciphertext memory.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
The separately linked [statistics contribution](coarse-statistics-kernels.md)
adds centered energy/variance, packed dot and partial reduction recipes. Its
intermediates pass through existing commands and back into contributed kernels
using the unchanged public runtime and native adapter.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
The separately linked [prepared matvec contribution](matvec-preparation.md)
adds an explicit reusable source artifact, complete dots, products and partial
reductions. Fixed-multiplier companions and rotation maps survive separate
requests and ordinary intermediate commands, without changing the runtime core.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
`test/install-consumer/rotation_contribution.cpp` is compiled separately using
only installed public headers. It registers `example.rotation-pair`, a
multi-output recipe composing two `native.rotate` requests that share one
caller-supplied preparation. The installed consumer also passes an immediate
result into an explicit compiled region. No core opcode or matcher edit is
needed for the contribution.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
`fhn-bench-runtime NATIVE_LIBRARY [REPS]` runs the existing `stats`,
`matvec-fused` and `matvec` corpus workloads in source order. The immediate and
prepared modes have compiler function pointers removed. The explicit region
mode uses the same imported mathematical operations and separately requests
compilation. All outputs and all logical slots are compared with the unchanged
independent corpus oracle on warmups and measured runs.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
The harness drops intermediates after their last use. Its timing includes
dispatch, allocation, arithmetic and temporary release, while excluding input
import, cryptographic setup, preparation and decryption. Preparation costs are
reported separately and must be added for one-shot use. Measurement order
rotates across modes. This is a comparison between paths of this project, not
an OpenFHE/SEAL/HEaaN benchmark. The explicit region example chooses a 32 MiB
reservation; it is not an automatically determined optimum.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
`stats` computes sums and scaled population variances of two 64-slot datasets;
`matvec-fused` computes an encrypted 8×8 matrix/vector example with eight
outputs; `matvec` is the existing cyclic rotation/scalar workload. Names do not
establish general application coverage.

documents.title: Contribution and validation
documents.text:
Remaining scope: CGGI↔CKKS/BFV conversions, cross-device events/residency,
automatic cross-command reuse discovery, a stable C plugin ABI for arbitrary
recipes and application-level encrypted control flow are not implemented.
This runtime exposes public orchestration and reusable resources; it does not
remove the cost of hidden data-dependent branches.

documents.title: Prepared matvec without changing the computation
documents.text:
Each dot performs the existing normalized ciphertext product and rotate-add
tree at distances 4, 2, 1. It consumes the same level and preserves the original
modular residues, scale and rounding decisions. No algebraic rewrite, compiler
request or hidden graph search is involved.

documents.title: What is reused
documents.text:
The immutable preparation owns a snapshot of the shared source and, according
to its flags, companion tables for fixed multipliers and rotation index maps.
A companion contains the quotient needed by the existing Shoup modular
multiplication primitive. Canonical normalization gives the same residue as
general modular multiplication, while avoiding division in the coefficient
loop. The prepared source and evaluation-key coefficients are reused by
multiple rows and separate requests.

documents.title: What is reused
documents.text:
The key flag also selects fixed-scalar Shoup arithmetic for P-lift/mod-down
and fused rescale. Those few scalar quotients are computed per invocation,
outside coefficient loops, rather than retained in the artifact. Consequently
its benchmark is explicitly **key companions plus per-call scalar hoisting**;
it does not isolate the gain from retained key state alone. The vector-only
and map-only modes isolate those retained components.

documents.title: Intermediate values remain ordinary values
documents.text:
`product` is an ordinary native ciphertext, independently usable by other
commands. The final request reuses the preparation's key companions and maps
for the remaining distances 2, 1. A product produced entirely by the existing
ordinary multiply command can also enter `contrib.matvec.reduce` at width 8.
The caller specifies the reduction boundary; the runtime does not infer it.

documents.title: Intermediate values remain ordinary values
documents.text:
Preparation requires a canonical two-component source at level >=1. Width must
be a power of two within its logical slots. A row must match source context,
basis, logical slots and scale. Reduction accepts the matching product level
and scale and preserves the actual intermediate metadata. This deliberately
bounded contract does not accept arbitrary mixed-scale matvec inputs.

documents.title: Ownership and limits
documents.text:
The contribution binds the source Value identity; a fresh same-shaped Value
cannot silently replace it. The native preparation is an independent snapshot,
so changing or freeing the original native source does not change the snapshot.
Weak key identities prevent preparation from retaining the client or its keys.
Every consumer obtains current matching key leases for its duration; expired
or replaced identities fail. Public wrappers retain context/library services.
Direct C callers must destroy preparation before its context and serialize
calls using that context, as for the other native APIs.

documents.title: Ownership and limits
documents.text:
The exact coefficient/map slab estimate is reserved before allocation. Runtime
budgets count the retained artifact, source dependency and full staging/output
buffers. Final publication still uses unchanged `NativeRuntime::importCopy`;
both staging and copy cost are included in the timings. Native consumers use
existing context scratch and allocate no heap. Metadata, allocator overhead,
keys, tables and context scratch are outside the retained-slab accounting.

documents.title: Ownership and limits
documents.text:
This first implementation owns companions per preparation. It does not dedupe
the same key tables across distinct prepared sources. The measured width-8
default artifact is several MiB; applications with many live prepared vectors
must account for that cost explicitly.

documents.title: Validation and measurement
documents.text:
The native/private tests compare every live residue against the unchanged
generic kernels across levels, key decomposition counts and preparation flags.
Provider tests check source identity, memory admission, lifecycle and ordinary
command boundaries. The installed consumer links the exported contribution
target using public headers only.

documents.title: Validation and measurement
documents.text:
`fhn-bench-runtime NATIVE_LIBRARY REPS matvec-reuse` runs the unchanged encrypted
8×8 corpus app with the generic paths, preparation ablations and both split
variants. Every warmup and timed execution checks all 64 logical output values
against the original independent oracle. All modes share ciphertexts and keys;
only the explicit region reference has compiler entrypoints available. Setup,
preparation, retained bytes and warm complete-app samples are reported
separately. See the [measurement report](matvec-preparation-validation-2026-10-31.md).

documents.title: Native CPU leveled RNS-CKKS
documents.text:
`ckks_fhn` performs genuine RLWE public-key encryption and homomorphic CKKS
arithmetic. Its evaluator operates on RNS polynomial ciphertexts and public
evaluation keys. It does not decrypt, retain a plaintext mirror, or
re-encrypt intermediate values. ToyFHE remains a separate insecure reference.

documents.title: Run
documents.text:
Use `libckks_fhn.so` on Linux. This 8×8 workload encrypts both matrix rows and
vector, verifies every output slot against the oracle, and compares native
`HMULT`/`HROT_ADD` with complete primitive decomposition. Required execution
fails on a skip. `ckks_fhn` also builds and installs with `BUILD_TEST=OFF`.
The existing C++ `Fhenon`/`Session` frontend and `fhn-bench-matvec` still use
the ToyFHE default; use the native FHN client API or corpus command above.

documents.title: Compiled applications
documents.text:
The optional [circuit API](circuit-execution.md) accepts value graphs and chooses
larger execution regions. It preserves levels for exact integer affine work,
combines compatible sums of products before one key switch/rescale, and reuses
prepared storage. `fhn-bench-circuit` executes ten current corpus apps on the
same default profile and checks every output slot. The raw opcode contracts
below remain unchanged and are useful as the comparison path.

documents.title: What is implemented
documents.text:
Each layer links only downward. L4 cannot include or link L5 key types.
Hybrid switching uses per-digit CRT projector messages `P * E_digit * s_old`
under the destination secret. Digit extension uses approximate BConv; removing
P and reconstructing decoded coefficients use exact centered CRT. Lower-level
switches retain the full key's original Q-to-P offsets.

documents.title: What is implemented
documents.text:
The encoder supports positive power-of-two real vector lengths up to N/2.
Short vectors repeat across physical slots, preserving signed cyclic rotations
of their logical length. Positive rotation steps rotate left. Decryption
requires the exact original logical count. Unsupported counts, nonfinite values,
coefficient-encoding overflow (int64 or centered active-Q range), incompatible
buffers, missing keys and depleted
levels fail rather than substituting another computation.

documents.title: What is implemented
documents.text:
On the raw opcode path, `MULT_CC` is a 2×2 tensor product with three output components. `RELINEARIZE`
returns two components; `RESCALE` removes one actual Q limb and divides the
scale. `HMULT` performs all three. Scalar multiplication also consumes one
level, even for integer and zero constants. Add/subtract require equal levels,
component counts and scales within relative 1e-12; there is no automatic scale
or level alignment. Plaintext-buffer and boolean/comparison opcodes are not
advertised. The circuit author remains responsible for numerical headroom.

documents.title: Client and evaluator lifetime
documents.text:
The additive `fhn_client_create/destroy/prepare/encrypt_vec_f64/decrypt_vec_f64`
exports keep ABI version 1 and the existing vtable layout intact. Native symbol
names have the `ckks_` prefix. It deliberately does not export the old
same-compute-context encryption/decryption functions.

documents.title: Client and evaluator lifetime
documents.text:
Create a compute context, then one client for it. `client_prepare(program)`
generates only the needed relinearization and Galois keys before execution.
The client owns the secret, public key, evaluation keys and its own workspace.
The compute context has no client or secret-key reference; it keeps weak
observers of evaluation keys, borrowed during one kernel call. Destroying the
client expires these keys: key-switching operations fail, while addition can
still execute. A compute context accepts only one client lifetime to prevent
accidental mixing of independent key identities. Buffers are checked against
their creating context. Free buffers and destroy the client before the context,
and unload the library last. Calls on one context must be serialized.

documents.title: Client and evaluator lifetime
documents.text:
`CorpusBackend` resolves the complete optional client group, prepares the
program and preserves that lifetime order, including move operations. Old
scalar/packed backend APIs remain supported. The installed-package smoke test
uses only installed public C-ABI headers and the installed native plugin to
perform an encrypted fractional square and a compiled scaled-square circuit.

documents.title: Default profile and boundaries
documents.text:
The default profile is N=8192 (4096 physical slots), three distinct Q primes
near 2^50, 2^40, 2^40, one P prime near 2^60, dnum=3, and scale=2^40. Every prime
is 1 modulo 2N. Fresh ciphertexts are level 2; two sequential `HMULT` operations
reach level 0. The prime search is deterministic; secret keys, errors, public
keys and encryption randomness come from the OS CSPRNG, never a fixed seed.
Secret/ephemeral polynomials are uniform ternary; errors use the difference
of two independent 21-bit population counts. Uniform residues use rejection
sampling. Entropy failure aborts the operation. Secret-key storage and key
operation sensitive scratch are wiped on release.

documents.title: Default profile and boundaries
documents.text:
Optional JSON fields are `log_degree`, `main_primes`, `aux_primes`, `dnum`,
and `log_default_scale`; unknown fields and unsupported profiles are rejected.
An empty object selects the default. Explicit prime arrays are decimal unsigned
integers. The adapter rejects sparse/terminal profiles and empty full-level
digits, and conservatively bounds the total QP bit length for degrees 1024
through 32768 using the public uniform-ternary 128-bit classical table in
[SEAL](https://github.com/microsoft/SEAL/blob/main/native/src/seal/util/hestdparms.h).
The default's conservative total is 190 bits against that table's 218-bit
N=8192 bound. This is parameter screening, not an independent security audit
or certification of this implementation.

documents.title: Default profile and boundaries
documents.text:
This is a leveled CPU implementation. Bootstrapping, general ciphertext
serialization and cross-process transport, GPU kernels, side-channel hardening,
sanitized/adversarial-result decryption and production security review remain
outside this version. No competitive latency or throughput claim is made.

documents.title: Memory accounting and validation
documents.text:
No successful evaluation kernel allocates from the heap or generates a key.
The caller supplies fixed output storage and an Arena. The adapter stages
results in its preallocated workspace so rejected operations and output aliases
do not corrupt existing buffers. `scratchBytes` figures are conservative
bounds including alignment, not exact minimum requirements. Setup explicitly
prepares tables for all configured levels; it does not lazily allocate during
execution.

documents.title: Memory accounting and validation
documents.text:
Each native buffer reserves three full-QP polynomials: 786432 bytes for the
default profile. Live two-component payload is 393216 bytes at level 2 and
shrinks to 131072 bytes at level 0, while reserved capacity stays unchanged.
`ckks_fhn_buffer_info` reports these separately along with workspace capacity
and observed high water. `fhn_level_bytes` reports the fixed reserve at every
valid level. The movement model excludes keys, tables and workspace; this CPU
backend does not physically evict memory, so modeled transfer counts/budgets
are not measured transfers or process-memory limits.

documents.title: Memory accounting and validation
documents.text:
Tests cover independent large-integer CRT oracles; key equations and noise
consistency across RNS limbs; fractional packing and full-Q decoding; randomized
public-key-only encryption and wrong-key mismatch; two sequential encrypted
multiplications; positive/negative/identity/conjugate rotations; multiple Q/P
primes per digit and lower levels; aliases, malformed metadata, scratch limits,
expired keys, entropy failure, secret wiping and zero successful-kernel heap
allocations. Native 8×8 output is checked against both a plaintext oracle and
primitive fallback. Whole-suite Debug, sanitizer and installed-package results
are recorded in the execution handoff rather than treated as a security proof.

documents.title: Native circuit execution
documents.text:
The optional circuit API describes application values and compiles them into a
reusable native CKKS execution plan. `MULTIPLY`, `SCALE`, and `ROTATE` are graph
semantics, not promises about kernel boundaries. The compiler can combine a
whole affine expression or a sum of products before choosing arithmetic and
storage. The existing `FhnProgram` opcode interface remains available with its
original physical semantics.

documents.title: Public API
documents.text:
1. `ckks_fhn_compile_circuit`: copy a graph and encrypted input signatures into
   an executable. Input values are not specialized into the plan.
2. `ckks_fhn_client_prepare_executable`: prepare the public evaluation keys
   required by that plan through the separate trusted client.
3. `ckks_fhn_run_executable`: bind input/output buffers and evaluate repeatedly.
4. `ckks_fhn_executable_stats`: report region counts and reserved slot/scratch
   bytes.
5. `ckks_fhn_executable_free`: release the plan before destroying its context.

documents.title: Public API
documents.text:
Calls on a context/executable are serialized by the caller. Inputs can be
re-encrypted or rebound if their owner, packing, level and scale match the
compiled signatures. Execution performs no heap allocation. Public outputs are
published after evaluation succeeds; input/output aliasing is allowed. Different
output values need different destination buffers. The client owns secret and
public evaluation-key objects; the evaluator retains only weak public-key
references and cannot decrypt. Destroying the client expires those keys.

documents.title: Public API
documents.text:
The circuit consists of explicit input IDs, topologically ordered value nodes,
and output IDs. Nodes support addition, subtraction, multiplication, scalar
scaling, scalar addition, negation, rotation and conjugation. The current native
lowering uses exact signed integer coefficients for affine regions; fractional
scaling uses a modulus-consuming path. Unsupported scale joins, insufficient
levels and out-of-range constants fail with diagnostics, without scale metadata
relabeling or a plaintext fallback. This first compiler bounds inputs plus nodes
and output ports to 65,536 each, affine forms to 256 terms, and recursive
materialization depth to 512; expressions exceeding these bounds are rejected
with diagnostics.

documents.title: Execution regions
documents.text:
Integer affine operations preserve level and scale. Compatible sums of products
can accumulate one three-component tensor and then perform one key switch and
rescale. Linear terms in such a region are lifted by the common scale using
modular arithmetic. Rotations can absorb compatible affine additions.

documents.title: Execution regions
documents.text:
The native multiplication kernel also combines auxiliary-modulus removal and
rescaling into one exact centered division. Its residues are tested against the
separate tensor/relinearize/rescale path on identical inputs and keys. This
bit-exact statement applies to that kernel rewrite; graph-level scheduling can
change CKKS rounding/noise while retaining the application accuracy contract.

documents.title: Execution regions
documents.text:
Storage slots are reused after their last consumers. A region destination never
overlaps live operands. Internal ciphertexts use their active Q basis and two
components; they need not reserve the public buffer's full three-component QP
capacity. `workspace_limit_bytes` bounds reserved internal slot and scratch
bytes. It excludes public I/O buffers, the backend's existing context scratch,
key/table storage, graph metadata, and allocator overhead; it is not a process
memory limit. Statistics report slot and scratch bytes separately.

documents.title: Corpus runner
documents.text:
`fhn-bench-circuit` imports the existing corpus's mathematical semantics into
circuits. This is an explicit application importer, not a generic rewrite of
arbitrary physical `FhnProgram` sequences. Explicit relinearize/rescale/level
operations and exact Boolean operations are rejected by that importer.

documents.title: Corpus runner
documents.text:
Use the platform's shared-library extension. Omit `--shape` to check the whole
corpus. `--require-execution` makes any skipped shape an error; zero executed
shapes or incorrect results always fail. `UNSUPPORTED` includes a compile
rejection such as an insufficient workspace budget, with the concrete reason.
`--workspace-bytes`, `--config`, `--atol` and `--rtol` control those explicit
constraints. Defaults are the native profile and `atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-6`.

documents.title: Corpus runner
documents.text:
An optional `--baseline /path/to/preserved/plugin` compares with the legacy
interpreter using preallocated SSA buffers. Timing alternates baseline/current
order, verifies all output slots before and after repetitions, and times only
completed evaluation. Context/client creation, encryption, compilation,
evaluation-key preparation and validation decryption are reported separately.
`decrypt_verify_ms` is total decryption time across verification passes.
Baseline execution failures are reported explicitly; an app newly enabled by
compilation has no baseline speedup. The plaintext oracle evaluates the original
corpus graph, independently of the imported circuit and native execution.

documents.title: Corpus runner
documents.text:
The current user-owned `examples/resnet_circuit.cpp` runs plaintext vectors and
ReLU, so it is not included as encrypted application evidence. The ordinary
`Fhenon`/`Session` frontend still defaults to its existing backend; using this
circuit path is explicit. This implementation does not add bootstrapping, GPU
execution, serialization, or a security certification.

documents.title: Contributed statistics and packed dot kernels
documents.text:
The separately linked `Fhenomenon::StatsKernels` target contributes four named
recipes. It uses the existing public runtime API and optional native CKKS
exports; neither `Runtime` nor `NativeRuntime` needs a new opcode, payload type,
dispatch branch, compiler pass or registry change.

documents.title: Contributed statistics and packed dot kernels
documents.text:
Attributes contain exactly `std::uint32_t width`, a nonzero power of two no
greater than the logical slot count. Partial reductions retain that slot count.
The native C implementation resides in its own translation unit and reuses
existing private region arithmetic. It does not invoke the circuit compiler.
The contribution registration/publication code lives outside the core library
in `contributions/stats/StatsKernels.cpp` and uses public headers only.

documents.title: Shared intermediate boundaries
documents.text:
The variance kernel consumes a sum made by ordinary commands; it does not
recompute or privately cache that sum. The caller retains it as another output.
The same computation can expose an intermediate and cross boundaries again:

documents.title: Shared intermediate boundaries
documents.text:
Here `energy` has two ordinary consumers, and their result re-enters another
contributed kernel. It is an ordinary native ciphertext Value with its actual
level/scale, not an opaque completed-app result. Similarly the original shared
vector in `matvec-fused` feeds eight contributed dot kernels without reimporting
or recomputing the input. A split variant performs the product and first
rotate/add with ordinary commands, then uses the contributed partial reduction.

documents.title: Arithmetic and supported envelope
documents.text:
This is the existing `stats` variance proxy, with its original four outputs
and independent oracle. Per dataset the new expression requires one tensor
product and one relinearization/rescale, compared with two of each originally.
The total number of rotations is unchanged. Fusing the product/reduction also
removes repeated public buffer allocation/publication and operation boundaries.

documents.title: Arithmetic and supported envelope
documents.text:
The initially considered expression `reduce(x*(width*x-s))` has a first-order
cancellation problem under CKKS error: constant -8 at width64 exceeded the
unchanged absolute tolerance. The centered-square form passed that regression
without changing tolerance. The benchmark still compares against the original
application oracle, not a newly defined encrypted-input oracle.

documents.title: Arithmetic and supported envelope
documents.text:
Division by width is represented explicitly by the actual output scale
`width * input_scale^2 / dropped_prime`. It consumes no extra Q level but uses
additional modulus headroom. The runtime does not force this value to have the
scale of an ordinary normalized product. Rotations and additions of matching
intermediates preserve the scale; incompatible joins are rejected.

documents.title: Arithmetic and supported envelope
documents.text:
Statistics recipes conservatively require level >= 2 (three active Q primes).
The tested statistics envelope is default native N8192, Q50/40/40, P60, dnum3,
width64 and input magnitudes <=8, with a correctly supplied sum. This admission
is not a precision guarantee for arbitrary parameters, magnitudes or malformed
sum provenance. Packed dot requires level >=1; reduction also supports level0,
subject to the usual CKKS value-range limits. Metadata cannot establish the
periodic plaintext or sum relationship.

documents.title: Ownership and accounting
documents.text:
Recipes retain their native context, adapter and library leases, never a client
or secret key. Applicability examines public capability and ciphertext metadata;
unavailable cases may fall through before execution. A native failure after
selection is reported without retrying another implementation.

documents.title: Ownership and accounting
documents.text:
Each invocation reserves a native staging ciphertext through `makeValue` before
allocation. After successful native execution, `importCopy` publishes the result
using the unchanged public native adapter. Both full allocations are charged
during this copy; staging is then released. This extra copy and allocation are
included in every timing. The native kernel itself allocates no heap memory and
uses the context's existing scratch. Scratch, evaluation keys and tables are
excluded from the runtime's retained-slab budget, as in the base runtime.

documents.title: Validation and measurement
documents.text:
`fhn-bench-runtime` retains the original immediate, shared-rotation-preparation
and explicit-region modes. It adds contributed and split modes for `stats` and
`matvec-fused`, plus `energy-only` for statistics: the same stable energy kernel
followed by a fully ordinary reduction. That last comparison separates algebraic
savings from larger-kernel boundary savings.

documents.title: Validation and measurement
documents.text:
Every timed iteration includes ordinary sum construction, contribution staging,
publication, dispatch, arithmetic and temporary release. Initial input import,
provider registration, optional preparation, encryption/decryption and final
output release are outside warm timing. Registration, input import, image load,
graph import and context/key/encryption setup are reported separately. All modes
register the same provider set and use identical ciphertexts/keys. Compiler
entrypoints are absent in every mode except the explicit region reference.

documents.title: Validation and measurement
documents.text:
The benchmark checks every logical output slot against the unchanged corpus
oracle. Native tests additionally encrypt/check all 4096 physical slots with
period-64 corpus and nearconstant data; separate constant regressions check all
64 logical slots. Installed-package
tests link the separate contribution target and exercise both shared-sum and
split-intermediate execution using installed public interfaces.

queries.text: How does the runtime select a registered recipe, and does it retry after execution fails?
암호화 평가 중 클라이언트를 없애면 공개 평가 키와 연산은 어떻게 되나요?
How are short real vectors packed into CKKS slots, and which direction is a positive rotation?
런타임의 보유 메모리 예산에는 무엇이 포함되고 키와 작업 공간도 포함되나요?
What does a reusable matvec preparation retain for the shared vector and evaluation keys?
명시적으로 회로를 컴파일할 때 입력 암호문을 재사용하거나 새 입력으로 바꿀 수 있나요?
Can I pass an ordinary encrypted intermediate into a contributed reduction kernel?
Is this CKKS implementation production audited, and does it support bootstrapping or cross-process ciphertext transport?
